title: The Best of Guru Dutt
description: Guru Dutt's essential directorial films, ranked by filmmaking quality, emotional depth, music, visual innovation, influence and lasting importance to Hindi cinema.
intro: The essential five, if you only watch five: Pyaasa, Kaagaz Ke Phool, Aar-Paar, Mr. & Mrs. 55 and Baazi.

entries.why_it_ranks: Guru Dutt's masterpiece — a devastating story of an unrecognized poet that combines romance, social criticism, extraordinary cinematography and S.D. Burman-Sahir Ludhianvi's immortal music.
A haunting film about fame, filmmaking, love and decline whose visual language was decades ahead of mainstream Hindi cinema.
Stylish, entertaining and remarkably modern, with Guru Dutt blending noir, romance, humour and O.P. Nayyar's superb music.
One of the great Hindi romantic comedies, using sparkling dialogue and Madhubala's wonderful performance to explore changing ideas about marriage and gender.
Guru Dutt's directorial debut helped establish Hindi film noir and demonstrated the visual sophistication that would define his later work.
An atmospheric crime-romance with morally complicated characters, striking imagery and memorable S.D. Burman music.
An unusual period adventure that shows Guru Dutt experimenting with scale, action and swashbuckling storytelling beyond his better-known urban dramas.
